quests.question: The meeting starts ___ 9:30 sharp.
quests.hint: This word pairs with an exact point on the clock.
quests.explanation: 'At' is used for precise clock times, treating them as a single fixed point.

quests.question: Her flight leaves ___ Thursday.
quests.hint: Days of the week take a different word than clock times do.
quests.explanation: 'On' is used with specific days, such as Thursday, unlike 'at', which is reserved for clock times.

quests.question: The festival takes place ___ July.
quests.hint: Months and years need a broader word than days or exact times.
quests.explanation: 'In' is used for longer periods like months and years, since a whole month can't be treated as one fixed point.

quests.question: Arrive ___ the doors open to get a good seat.
quests.hint: Getting there needs to happen earlier than that event, not at the same time.
quests.explanation: 'Before' places one event earlier in time than another — arriving must happen ahead of the doors opening.

quests.question: We'll grab coffee ___ the workshop ends.
quests.hint: This is the opposite direction in time from the previous example.
quests.explanation: 'After' places one event later than another — the coffee happens once the workshop is finished.

quests.question: Submit the form ___ Friday to avoid a late fee.
quests.hint: The deadline is a day that hasn't arrived yet, not an ongoing state.
quests.explanation: 'Before' shows the form must be submitted earlier than Friday, matching the same logic taught with the earlier example.

quests.question: She fell asleep ___ the movie.
quests.hint: Name the event first, then this word slots in front of it, not a length of time.
quests.explanation: 'During' is followed by a noun naming an event or period, like a movie. 'While' would need a full clause instead of a noun, which doesn't fit here.

quests.question: They've lived here ___ three years.
quests.hint: This word is followed by a length of time, not a named event.
quests.explanation: 'For' pairs with a quantity of time, such as three years, showing how long something has lasted.

quests.question: The store closes early ___ public holidays.
quests.hint: Public holidays are treated as a named period here, not a number of days.
quests.explanation: 'During' fits because 'public holidays' names a period rather than stating its length — 'for' would need a duration like 'for two days' instead.

quests.question: I haven't seen him ___ last spring.
quests.hint: Last spring is a starting point in the past, not a length of time.
quests.explanation: 'Since' marks the starting point of a period that continues to now — last spring is when the gap began.

quests.question: We've been waiting ___ almost an hour.
quests.hint: An hour is a length of time, not a fixed starting point.
quests.explanation: 'For' is used with a length of time, such as almost an hour, showing the duration of the wait.

quests.question: She has worked at the hospital ___ 2015.
quests.hint: A specific year works as a starting point here, just like 'last spring' earlier.
quests.explanation: 'Since' fits because 2015 is treated as the starting point of an ongoing situation, matching the pattern from the first example in this level.

quests.question: Please send the report ___ Friday, at the latest.
quests.hint: Something needs to be finished no later than this point, not kept going up to it.
quests.explanation: 'By' marks a deadline for completing an action — the phrase 'at the latest' is a strong clue that a single finished action is expected, not a continuous state.

quests.question: The office stays open ___ 8 PM, so you can drop by anytime before then.
quests.hint: This describes a state that continues right up to that time, not a task finished by then.
quests.explanation: 'Until' shows a situation continuing up to a point in time — the office remains open the whole time, not just completed by 8 PM.

quests.question: I'll be stuck in meetings ___ 3 o'clock, so let's talk after that.
quests.hint: The meetings don't end early — they run all the way up to that hour.
quests.explanation: 'Until' fits because the meetings continue right up to 3 o'clock, the same continuous idea taught with the office hours example.

quests.question: Refunds are processed ___ five business days.
quests.hint: This sets an outer limit that something must happen inside of.
quests.explanation: 'Within' shows an action will happen inside a given time limit, such as five business days, rather than describing its exact length.

quests.question: The baby cried nonstop ___ the flight, from takeoff to landing.
quests.hint: The clue about takeoff and landing shows the whole span was affected, start to finish.
quests.explanation: 'Throughout' emphasizes that something continued across the entire period without a break, matching the 'takeoff to landing' detail.

quests.question: You can cancel the order ___ 24 hours of purchase.
quests.hint: Like the refund example, this sets a limit for when the action can still happen.
quests.explanation: 'Within' fits again here, marking 24 hours as the outer boundary for canceling the order.

quests.question: The store is open ___ 9 to 5 on weekdays.
quests.hint: This word marks the starting point of the range, paired later with 'to'.
quests.explanation: 'From' marks the beginning of a time range, working together with 'to' to show the full span of opening hours.

quests.question: The conference is scheduled ___ March 3rd.
quests.hint: A specific date works like a specific day of the week.
quests.explanation: 'On' is used for specific dates, just as it is for days of the week like Thursday.

quests.question: The sale continues ___ Friday, so there's still time to grab a discount.
quests.hint: The sale is still running now and will keep going up to that day.
quests.explanation: 'Until' shows an ongoing situation lasting up to a point — 'continues until' is standard, while 'continues by' or 'continues to' aren't natural phrasings here.

quests.question: The invoice must be paid ___ the end of the month.
quests.hint: Financial deadlines like this one usually pair with the same word used for the report earlier.
quests.explanation: 'By' is the standard word for financial and administrative deadlines, marking the latest acceptable point for payment.

quests.question: Please silence your phones ___ the presentation.
quests.hint: Name the event, then this word goes in front of it.
quests.explanation: 'During' takes a noun naming an event, like a presentation — 'while' would require a full clause instead.

quests.question: Ticket prices have risen ___ last year.
quests.hint: Last year marks the point when the rise began, not its length.
quests.explanation: 'Since' marks the starting point of an ongoing change — prices have kept rising from that point until now.

quests.question: I've known her ___ we were in college together.
quests.hint: No length of time is given — only a moment when the friendship began.
quests.explanation: 'Since' fits because the sentence names a starting event, not a duration; 'for' would require a stated length, like 'for ten years'.

quests.question: Keep the leftovers refrigerated ___ they're eaten.
quests.hint: This describes a state lasting up to an event, not a single deadline moment.
quests.explanation: 'Until' shows the leftovers should stay refrigerated continuously up to the moment they're eaten; 'by' doesn't fit smoothly before a clause like this.

quests.question: He was in a coma ___ two weeks after the accident.
quests.hint: A specific length of time is stated here, not a named period.
quests.explanation: 'For' is correct because 'two weeks' is a duration; 'during' would need a defined period like 'during his recovery' rather than a number of weeks.

quests.question: By the time we finally boarded, we'd been standing in line ___ over three hours.
quests.hint: A stretch of time is named, not a starting moment or a named event.
quests.explanation: 'For' fits because 'over three hours' is a duration, describing how long the standing in line lasted.

quests.question: The museum offers free admission ___ the first Sunday of every month.
quests.hint: This is a specific day, even though it's described in relation to the month.
quests.explanation: 'On' is used because 'the first Sunday' still names a specific day, the same rule that applies to any day of the week.

quests.question: Renovations will continue ___ the new wing opens next spring.
quests.hint: The work keeps going all the way up to that future event.
quests.explanation: 'Until' shows the renovations continuing right up to the opening — 'by' would wrongly suggest the renovations are the thing being completed at that point, not an ongoing process.
